Asset: WELL-0008 (SW-23 Well 008, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 03 Feb 2023 08:00 · Finished: 04 Feb 2023 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 28 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0008-0016 on 2023-02-02 Report written: 05 Feb 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0008-0016 at 09:00 on 2023-02-02 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.6% of the pad area, estimated 1.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 7.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0008-018

Asset: WELL-0008 (SW-23 Well 008, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 04 Oct 2024 08:00 · Finished: 09 Oct 2024 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 118 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0008-0102 on 2024-10-03 Report written: 10 Oct 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0008-0102 showed the wellhead at 26.5 °C with the air at 26.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0008-018 (WS-06).
